Takashima is known as the place where the Mongol fleet was struck by a storm during the Mongol invasions of the Kamakura period (the Koan campaign), and Mongol ships and relics have been found on the surrounding seabed. From the hilltop park you can view the Genkai Sea and Imari Bay and reflect on these waters, once the scene of fierce battle.
quiz_en: What is the name for the events of the Kamakura period when great Mongol armies twice attempted to invade Japan?

desc_en: This roadside station in the Takashima area of Matsuura City sits at the foot of the Takashima Hizen Bridge, which links Takashima with Karatsu City in Saga Prefecture. Takashima is a historic island known as a stage of the Mongol invasions, and fisheries such as tiger pufferfish farming thrive in the surrounding waters. Island specialties and fresh seafood are on sale, making it perfect for a break on a drive. Take a breather while gazing at the bridge and the blue sea.
quiz_en: What is the name of the large bridge near this roadside station that connects Takashima with Karatsu City in Saga Prefecture?

desc_en: Makinodake Historic Park, in the Misato district in the center of Takashima, is built on the island's high ground. Takashima is known as an old battlefield of the Mongol invasions, and historic sites and place names conveying that era remain across the island. From the park you can see the calm sea surrounding the island and the islands nearby. Amid peaceful island scenery, let your thoughts turn to the distant history of the Kamakura period.
quiz_en: If you toured the historic sites of Takashima, stage of the Mongol invasions, which event of that time would you most like to learn about?

desc_en: This is Enryo-ji in Hotokezaka, in the Imafuku area of Matsuura City. Imafuku is a seaside town facing Imari Bay, with a station on the Matsuura Railway. The Matsuura area is known as the land where a samurai band called the "Matsuura-to" was active in medieval times. Bring your hands together in the quiet, green grounds and reflect on the history and lives of the people of Matsuura, who have walked alongside the sea.
quiz_en: What was the name of the medieval band of samurai who were based in the Matsuura region and active on the seas?

desc_en: Spreading across central Tsushima, Aso Bay is a scenic spot with an intricately indented ria coastline and is part of Iki-Tsushima Quasi-National Park. The scenery woven by islands and inlets of all sizes is tranquil, and pearl farming is carried out here. On the south shore remain the ruins of Kaneda Castle, an ancient mountain fortress built in the Asuka period. Enjoy the view from the observation decks or a cruise around the bay.
quiz_en: What is the name for a complex, indented coastline like Aso Bay's, formed when mountainous land sank into the sea?

desc_en: Watatsumi Shrine, facing Aso Bay on Tsushima, is an ancient shrine dedicated to the sea goddess Toyotama-hime and Hikohohodemi. Torii gates stand in a line from the front of the main hall toward the sea, and at high tide you can see the magical sight of their bases submerged in water. As a place linked to the myth of Umisachi and Yamasachi, it preserves a "Ryugu legend" of the undersea palace and is wrapped in a mystical atmosphere.
quiz_en: At Watatsumi Shrine, what appears to stand in the middle of the sea when the tide is high?

desc_en: Saruiwa, on the Kurosaki Peninsula in the Gonoura area of western Iki Island, is a basalt rock jutting into the sea. Its name, meaning "Monkey Rock," comes from its shape, which looks just like the profile of a monkey looking away, and it has become Iki's signature sightseeing spot. The surrounding coast is lined with cliffs, creating a superb contrast with the blue Genkai Sea. Try changing your viewing angle to find the monkey's face.
quiz_en: Saruiwa, one of Iki's most famous sights, is known for resembling a monkey in what kind of pose?

desc_en: Nanatsugama Limestone Cave in the Saikai area of Saikai City is designated a national Natural Monument. It was formed over many years as limestone layers that built up on the ancient seabed were eroded, and inside you can see formations such as stalactites and stalagmites. The cool cave stays chilly even in summer, letting you enjoy the mysterious underground world as if on an expedition.
quiz_en: Stalactites hang down from the ceiling of a limestone cave. What are the formations that grow up from the floor called?

desc_en: Isanoura Park in the Saikai area of Saikai City is a nature park centered on the reservoir of Isanoura Dam. There are a campground and cottages by the lake, and you can also enjoy waterside activities such as canoeing. Its quiet setting surrounded by forest and the lake's changing look through the seasons are its appeal. Get active outdoors and refresh yourself in nature.
quiz_en: If you went camping beside a lake like the one at Isanoura Park, which outdoor activity would you most like to try?

desc_en: Spanning the Hario Strait at the entrance to Omura Bay, between Sasebo City and Saikai City, Saikai Bridge is an arch bridge completed in 1955. Strong currents form beneath the bridge with the rising and falling tides, and during spring tides large whirlpools can be seen. The New Saikai Bridge stands next to it, and from its walkway you can look down on the whirlpools. In spring the surrounding parks are colored by cherry blossoms.
quiz_en: In the Hario Strait beneath Saikai Bridge, what phenomenon can be seen when the difference between high and low tide is large?

desc_en: Shihondo Park in the Seihi area of Saikai City is a nature-rich park facing Omura Bay. It has a campground and cottages, so you can enjoy the outdoors while gazing at the calm bay. Omura Bay has only a narrow connection to the open sea, and because its waves are gentle it is also called the "Sea of the Koto," after the Japanese harp. Enjoy waterside walks and play by the sea, and watch the sun set over the bay.
quiz_en: Because of its calm, gentle waves, Omura Bay is known by a beautiful nickname. What is this poetic name?

desc_en: Oshima Bridge Park in the Oshima area of Saikai City lies at the foot of the Oshima Bridge, which connects the Nishisonogi Peninsula with Oshima Island. From the high ground you can take in the majestic bridge spanning the strait and the blue sea dotted with islands. Oshima once flourished with coal mining and is now known as an island of shipbuilding. Feel the sea breeze while gazing at the scenery woven by bridge and sea.
quiz_en: When it comes to a bridge across the sea like the Oshima Bridge, would you rather drive across it or admire it on foot?

desc_en: This seaside park is in Yukiura, in the Oseto area of Saikai City. Yukiura is a small community facing the East China Sea, with a beautiful sandy beach spreading out where the Yukiura River meets the sea. It is also known as a surfing spot, and many people have moved to the area drawn by its rich nature. Summer swimming is a given, but watching the sun sink into the sea is also exceptional.
quiz_en: Whether surfing or swimming, how would you most like to enjoy a day at the sea in Yukiura?

desc_en: Tsugane Otoshi Falls, in the hills of Yukiura in the Oseto area of Saikai City, is a waterfall on the upper reaches of the Yukiura River. The surroundings are wrapped in lush forest, and the sound of water tumbling down the rock face echoes pleasantly. In summer it is a place where people come to cool off. Follow the river upstream from the Yukiura community at its mouth and feel the nature of Yukiura, where mountains and sea connect.
quiz_en: At a forest waterfall like Tsugane Otoshi Falls, which would you most like to experience, the sound of the water or the cool breeze?

desc_en: On Mount Fugen, part of Mount Unzen, volcanic activity that began in 1990 erupted large amounts of lava, and a lava dome grew. This dome was named "Heisei Shinzan" and is now the highest peak of Mount Unzen. The pyroclastic flows that accompanied the eruption caused great damage. From places such as Nita Pass you can see the rugged lava slopes up close and feel the power of the volcano.
quiz_en: What name was given to the lava dome that grew during the eruption of Mount Fugen beginning in 1990?

name_en: Unzen Jigoku and Unzen Onsen Baths
desc_en: Unzen Jigoku (Unzen Hells), at the heart of Unzen Onsen, is a dramatic geothermal area where white steam rises and the smell of sulfur fills the air. Walking the trails, you can see hot water and steam spouting up close. It also has a sad history as a place where Christians were persecuted in the Edo period. Taste onsen eggs cooked in the steam of the hells and soak in the famous hot springs.
quiz_en: What are the eggs boiled in geothermal steam, a famous specialty of Unzen Jigoku, called?

desc_en: The Hara Castle Ruins in Minamishimabara City are where rebels led by Amakusa Shiro barricaded themselves during the Shimabara-Amakusa Rebellion in the early Edo period. Surrounded by a huge shogunate army, the castle fell after fierce fighting. It is a component of the World Heritage site "Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region." Stand on the site of the main keep overlooking the Ariake Sea and reflect on the beginning of the era of hidden faith.
quiz_en: Who was the young commander who led the rebels barricaded in Hara Castle during the Shimabara-Amakusa Rebellion?

desc_en: Nakao Castle Park in Nagayo Town is a hilltop park built on the site of a former castle. Nagayo lies just north of Nagasaki City and has developed as a commuter town facing Omura Bay. It is also known as a "mikan town" with a history of growing unshu mandarin oranges. Enjoy a relaxing time while taking in the view from the hilltop park.
quiz_en: Nagayo Town, home of Nakao Castle Park, is known for its history of growing which kind of fruit?

desc_en: Sakino Nature Park in the Nishitogitsu area of Togitsu Town is a nature park spreading across a cape that juts into Omura Bay. A walking path runs along the calm coastline of the bay, so you can enjoy a stroll in the sea breeze. Many people come to explore tide pools or fish, and although it is close to central Nagasaki, rich nature remains. At dusk the bay turns a deep red, creating a beautiful view.
quiz_en: If you went exploring the rocky tide pools at a cape nature park, which sea creature would you most like to find?

desc_en: Yakimono Park in Hasami Town is an outdoor park displaying reproductions of historic kilns from around the world. Hasami has been a pottery town since the Edo period, mass-producing everyday tableware for ordinary people, and its products are now popular as "Hasami ware." A facility next to the park also exhibits and sells tableware. Compare the different shapes of the kilns.
quiz_en: In the Edo period, inexpensive rice bowls mass-produced in Hasami were sold from boats on the Yodo River. What were they called?

desc_en: This hot spring is in Hasami Town, a town of pottery. Hasami is a hilly town in central Nagasaki Prefecture known as a home of ceramics, and beautiful countryside scenery such as the Oniki terraced rice fields also spreads out here. After hunting for tableware on a tour of potteries or strolling around town, rest your body slowly in the hot spring and bring your Hasami trip to a relaxed close.
quiz_en: If you took home one piece of Hasami ware tableware, what kind of dish would you like to serve on it?

desc_en: Sarayama Park in the Ichinose area of Saza Town is a park loved by local people. Saza lies just north of Sasebo City, a nature-rich town with the Saza River flowing through its center. "Sarayama" is also known in Kyushu as a word meaning a pottery kiln site. Stroll while enjoying seasonal flowers and greenery, and savor the town's peaceful atmosphere.
quiz_en: What is the name of the river that flows through the center of Saza Town and is known for its rows of cherry trees?

desc_en: These are the Kawazu cherry trees blooming along the Saza River in Saza Town. Kawazu-zakura is an early-blooming cherry that flowers before the Somei-yoshino variety, characterized by its deep pink blossoms. The rows of flowers coloring the riverside while the air is still chilly let you feel spring arriving a little early. The scene where yellow rapeseed blossoms overlap with pink cherry blossoms is also charming, making a riverside walk even more enjoyable.
quiz_en: The Kawazu cherry is named after the town of Kawazu. In which prefecture of Japan is the town of Kawazu located?

desc_en: Towering in the center of Kumamoto City, Kumamoto Castle was built by Kato Kiyomasa and is one of Japan's three great castles. It is renowned for its "mushagaeshi" stone walls, which curve outward more steeply toward the top, and it proved impregnable even in the Satsuma Rebellion. Though heavily damaged in the 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes, the main keep has been restored, and reconstruction continues today. It is also fondly called Ginnan Castle (Ginkgo Castle).
quiz_en: What is the name of the distinctive shape of Kumamoto Castle's stone walls, which curve outward more steeply toward the top?

desc_en: Suizenji Jojuen in Kumamoto City is a Momoyama-style stroll garden created by the Hosokawa family, lords of the Kumamoto domain. Centered on a pond fed by spring water from underground streams flowing from Aso, its landscape is said to be modeled on the 53 Stations of the Tokaido, and an artificial hill styled after Mount Fuji catches the eye. The garden also contains Izumi Shrine, which enshrines successive Hosokawa lords. Enjoy the clear water and green scenery.
quiz_en: The artificial hill in Suizenji Jojuen Garden is said to be modeled on which mountain, the highest in Japan?

desc_en: Tatsuta Nature Park, at the foot of Mount Tatsuta in Chuo Ward, Kumamoto City, was built on the site of Taisho-ji, the family temple of the Hosokawa clan. In the park is the "Yotsu Gobyo," the graves of the first Hosokawa lord Fujitaka and his wife and the second lord Tadaoki and his wife Gracia. A mossy garden, bamboo grove and tea house remain in this quiet space wrapped in greenery. Stroll and feel Kumamoto's history.
quiz_en: Who is the woman resting in Tatsuta Nature Park, the wife of Hosokawa Tadaoki, also known as a Christian of the Warring States period?

desc_en: This autumn grand festival is held every September at Fujisaki Hachimangu in Kumamoto City. The sacred procession includes the "Zuibyo" parade, in which decorated horses and young men called seko march along chanting "Dokai, dokai," filling the city of Kumamoto with excitement. It is Kumamoto's signature autumn festival, with bold decorated horses advancing through town to the sound of trumpets and drums.
quiz_en: At the Fujisaki Hachimangu festival, what distinctive chant do the seko shout as they follow the decorated horses?

desc_en: Tsukahara Kofun Park in the Jonan area of Minami Ward, Kumamoto City, preserves the Tsukahara Kofun Group, a cluster of many burial mounds including round, square and keyhole-shaped tombs, and is a national Historic Site. It was discovered during surveys for expressway construction, and the route was changed to preserve it. The scene of grass-covered mounds in a row is peaceful, letting you feel close to the lives of ancient people.
quiz_en: Besides round and square mounds, what is the name of the representative keyhole-shaped type of ancient burial mound in Japan?

desc_en: This is the autumn grand festival of Kawashiri Jingu Shrine in the Kawashiri district of Minami Ward, Kumamoto City. Kawashiri was a port town that thrived on boat transport along the Midori and Kase rivers, home to the Kumamoto domain's storehouses, and old streets and warehouses remain today. The tradition of blade-making also lives on, known as "Kawashiri cutlery." Walk the historic streets bustling with the festival and feel the prosperity of the past.
quiz_en: What famous products, such as kitchen knives, are traditionally made in the Kawashiri district of Kumamoto City?

desc_en: Tabaruzaka, in the Ueki area of Kita Ward, Kumamoto City, was the site of the fiercest fighting of the Satsuma Rebellion in 1877. Government forces and the Satsuma army led by Saigo Takamori fought a fierce battle here for 17 days. The folk song "Tabaruzaka" sings, "The rain keeps falling, the men and horses are soaked." The park has a museum that conveys the history of the battle through features such as a house marked by bullet holes.
quiz_en: What is the name of the Meiji-era samurai rebellion led by Saigo Takamori that made Tabaruzaka a scene of fierce fighting?

desc_en: The Himuro Festival is held at Yatsushiro Shrine (Myoken-gu) in the Myoken area of Yatsushiro City. A himuro is an icehouse used to store winter ice and snow until summer in the days before refrigerators. Yatsushiro Shrine is fondly called "Myoken-san" by locals, and its autumn Myoken Festival is a national Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, also inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list. Visit its grounds surrounded by greenery.
quiz_en: Which autumn festival of Yatsushiro Shrine features the "Game," a mythical beast combining a turtle and a snake?

desc_en: This autumn leaves festival is held throughout the Gokanosho area of Izumi, Yatsushiro City. Gokanosho is a remote area deep in the Kyushu Mountains, with legends that fleeing Heike warriors and descendants of Sugawara no Michizane lived here in hiding. In autumn the mountains turn red and yellow, and you can enjoy magnificent foliage along with suspension bridges over the gorges and old residences such as the Ogata and Saza family houses.
quiz_en: According to Gokanosho legend, which group of people fled deep into the mountains to live in hiding after the Battle of Dan-no-ura?

desc_en: Eikoku-ji in Hitoyoshi City is known as the "Ghost Temple." It holds a hanging scroll of a ghost said to have been painted by a head priest in the Edo period, and many people visit to see it. A story about the ghost is also linked to the pond on the grounds. Hitoyoshi is a castle town on the Kuma River, also famous for Kuma shochu and river rafting. Encounter this mysterious tale in the quiet grounds.
quiz_en: What is depicted on the eerie and mysterious hanging scroll handed down at Eikoku-ji Temple in Hitoyoshi City?

desc_en: This is Sekisui-ji in the Shimoharada area of Hitoyoshi City. Hitoyoshi is a castle town ruled by the Sagara clan for about 700 years, and many temples and shrines linked to the Sagara remain in the city. Sekisui-ji is a quiet temple wrapped in mountain greenery, where you can worship at your leisure in a calm atmosphere. Enjoy the spring and autumn scenery as you feel the history and nature of the Hitoyoshi Basin.
quiz_en: Which daimyo clan ruled Hitoyoshi, home of Sekisui-ji, for a very long time until the end of the Edo period?

desc_en: Nobara Hachimangu in Arao City has long drawn worshippers as the guardian shrine of the region. At its autumn grand festival, a performing art called "furyu" is offered, known as a tradition handed down since long ago. Arao faces the Ariake Sea, and places that convey its coal mining history remain, such as the World Heritage-listed Manda Pit. Take a leisurely walk through the historic grounds.
quiz_en: Which former coal mine in Arao City is a component of the World Heritage site "Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution"?

desc_en: The Araen Festival is held around a large shopping complex in Arao City. Arao sits at the northwestern tip of Kumamoto Prefecture, facing the Ariake Sea, and once thrived as part of the Miike coal mine. Many people gather for the festival, and the summer night is brightened with dancing, stage shows and fireworks. Fully enjoy the atmosphere of this energetic local festival.
quiz_en: At a summer festival, what gets you most excited, the dancing, the fireworks or the food stalls?

desc_en: This spring grand festival is held at Yotsuyama Shrine in the Oshima area of Arao City. Fondly called "Yotsuyama-san," the shrine draws many worshippers as a deity of business prosperity and good fortune. It stands atop the small hill of Yotsuyama, and from its grounds you can see the Ariake Sea. On festival days, stalls line the grounds and the approach, making it a spring tradition bustling with local people.
quiz_en: If you went to the Yotsuyama Shrine festival, what would be the first thing you would buy from the stalls along the approach?

desc_en: Yunoko Onsen in Minamata City is a seaside hot spring resort facing the Shiranui Sea. You can soak while viewing small islands floating on the calm sea, and at dusk the setting sun shines beautifully, dyeing the sea deep red. The surrounding waters are highly transparent, and you can also enjoy sea fishing and boat tours. Feel the sea breeze and spend a moment unique to a seaside hot spring.
quiz_en: Which sea does Yunoko Onsen face, known for a legend about mysterious lights that appear on its waters?

desc_en: Yunotsuru Onsen, along the Yude River in the hills of Minamata City, is a hot spring long loved as a place for therapeutic bathing. It is a simple hot spring town with inns along the river, filled with the charm of a peaceful mountain village. The area is surrounded by lush nature, and the murmur of the river is pleasant to the ear. Let a quiet mountain hot spring slowly heal both body and mind.
quiz_en: At a mountain hot spring like Yunotsuru Onsen, which glowing creature would you be delighted to see by the river on a summer night?

desc_en: The "Koiryu Festival" is a summer festival held in Minamata City. Minamata, at the southernmost tip of Kumamoto Prefecture facing the Shiranui Sea, is blessed with hot springs and the nature of both sea and mountains. The festival features dancing and fireworks, and the town is busy with crowds. As an Environmental Model City, Minamata is also working on town development that values the environment. Enjoy the excitement of a summer night.
quiz_en: If you joined Minamata's summer festival, which would you rather wear, a yukata cotton robe or a happi festival coat?

desc_en: This is Hanegi Hachimangu in the Hanegi area of Tamana City. Tamana developed along the lower reaches of the Kikuchi River and has long prospered as a hub of transportation and trade. The shrine is beloved by local people, and its grounds are wrapped in a calm atmosphere. After your visit, enjoy nearby Tamana Onsen and the local specialty, Tamana ramen, as you explore the town.
quiz_en: What is the name of the river that flows through Tamana City into the Ariake Sea and was long used for boat transport?

desc_en: Tamana Onsen, spreading across the Ryuganji area of Tamana City, is a historic hot spring known since long ago. In the hot spring town on the banks of the Kikuchi River, ryokan and hotels line the streets, and there are also facilities for day visitors. Tamana is also known for Tamana ramen, with a tonkotsu pork-bone broth flavored with garlic. After your bath, enjoy this local specialty.
quiz_en: After a soak at Tamana Onsen, you might try Tamana ramen. What kind of soup is this local specialty ramen made with?

desc_en: Yamaga Onsen, which springs up in central Yamaga City, is a hot spring town that also prospered as a post town on the Buzen Kaido highway in the Edo period. The town's symbol, "Sakura-yu," is a public bathhouse that originated as an Edo-period lord's rest house, and its stately wooden building has been restored. In summer the "Yamaga Toro Festival" is held, where women dance with golden lanterns on their heads, creating a magical scene.
quiz_en: At the Yamaga Toro Festival, what color are the lanterns that the women wear on their heads while they dance?

desc_en: Hirayama Onsen in Yamaga City is a quiet hot spring area with inns scattered across the farmland of the hills. Its water is known for its silky feel and is said to leave your skin smooth after bathing. Many of the ryokan have open-air baths or private baths, letting you enjoy the water at leisure surrounded by nature. In this hideaway hot spring far from the bustle, let your body and mind relax.
quiz_en: If you could take a private open-air bath at Hirayama Onsen, who would you most like to go there with?

desc_en: This is Kikuka Onsen in the Kikuka area of Yamaga City. Kikuka is a peaceful area surrounded by mountains and farmland, and it is also known for growing grapes for wine. Nearby are the ruins of Kikuchi Castle, an ancient mountain fortress, where the reconstructed octagonal drum tower is a highlight. After touring the historic site and strolling the countryside, relax with a sigh of relief in the hot spring.
quiz_en: What is the reconstructed octagonal building at the ruins of Kikuchi Castle, an ancient mountain fortress in Kikuka, called?

desc_en: This is Kamoto Onsen in the Kamoto area of Yamaga City. Kamoto is a farming town in the Kikuchi River basin, and its Kutami district is known for producing shibu uchiwa fans. This hot spring, surrounded by peaceful countryside, is also loved by locals. Try a hot spring tour, combining it with other distinctive hot springs in Yamaga City such as Yamaga Onsen and Hirayama Onsen.
quiz_en: What traditional craft coated with persimmon tannin has long been made in the Kutami district of Kamoto?

desc_en: Sagara-ji in the Kikuka area of Yamaga City is a temple fondly known as "Sagara Kannon," worshipped as a Kannon of safe childbirth and child-rearing. Many worshippers come to its quiet grounds in the hills with their wishes, conveying the depth of people's prayers. The surroundings are a lush mountain village where you can enjoy the scenery of each season. Calm your mind in the peaceful village of Kikuka.
quiz_en: Sagara-ji Temple is affectionately known as "Sagara ___." Which Buddhist deity's name fills in the blank?

desc_en: This azalea festival is held at Nichirinji Park in the Sugi area of Yamaga City. Many azaleas are planted in the park spreading across the grounds of Nichirin-ji Temple, and in spring the mountain slopes are covered with red, pink and white flowers. Nichirin-ji is also known as a temple linked to the 47 ronin of Ako. Enjoy spring in Yamaga as you walk through the vivid carpet of flowers.
quiz_en: What flower colors the mountain slopes red and pink during the spring festival at Nichirinji Park?

desc_en: This Shokonsai is held in the Kutami district of the Kamoto area of Yamaga City. Shokonsai is an event to console the spirits of the war dead and renew prayers for peace, and it has been carefully handed down by local people. Kutami is also known as a town producing shibu uchiwa, fans coated with persimmon tannin. Take in the town on the festival day and feel the prayers and lives of the local people.
quiz_en: Like Kutami's traditional persimmon-tannin fans, what kind of traditional craft would you like to buy and bring home from a trip?

desc_en: Located northwest of the Aso outer caldera rim, Kikuchi Gorge is at the source of the Kikuchi River. Waterfalls and pools of all sizes line the stream surrounded by virgin forest, and the clear water flowing here has been chosen as one of Japan's 100 best waters. The water stays cold even in summer, so people come seeking a natural air conditioner. In autumn the leaves color the gorge vividly, and it bustles with tourists.
quiz_en: What is the name of the nationwide selection of Japan's finest waters that includes the clear water of Kikuchi Gorge?
